thread:
incident-bot: :warning: ALERT: GPU queue growth detected for model redwood-3b-io. queue_length ↑ 8x in 2m, autoscaler at max_nodes=8 (scale cap). Throttles rising, 429s observed. Paging oncall @Mia.
Mia: oncall here, looking. can someone paste the recent deploys/rollouts?
Oliver: grabbing metrics — one sec. seen a big jump at 08:12 UTC.
Oliver: quick snapshot:
```
model=redwood-3b-io | queue_len: baseline 40 -> 320
prefix_cache_hitrate: 92% -> 13%
avg_token_latency: 120ms -> 450ms
autoscaler_nodes: 8/8 (cap)
throttle_rate: 0.3 -> 2.1 req/s
```
Anna: FYI we rolled batching/continuous batching config at 08:10 as part of canary for PR #4521. changed `continuous_batching.window_ms` and enabled `kv_prefix_ttl=30s` in the same rollout.
Mia: ok that timing lines up. if prefix cache hitrate collapsed, throughput would plummet and queues blow up.
Devon: can we temporarily lift the autoscale cap while we investigate? set to 16 and watch.
Mia: @Devon do it. also what's the customer impact right now?
CS-Bot: Monitoring summary: ~12 customers hitting elevated tail latencies; 3 customers seeing 5xx/429 for small percentage (~0.7%) of requests in last 5m. No SLO breach yet but trending.
Devon: running scale cap bump:
```
# aws/internal API
POST /platform/autoscaler/config
{ "model":"redwood-3b-io", "max_nodes":16 }
```
Devon: update submitted. should take ~30-60s to reconcile.
incident-bot: ACTION: autoscaler config change applied at 3654321032 by Devon.
Oliver: watching queue — slight drop but still high. prefix cache still low.
Anna: I can roll back the batching part of the canary to the previous values (the TTL tweak likely caused prefix entries to expire faster). rollback PR #4521 batching chunk only.
Mia: do it. prefer rollback over further traffic risk.
Anna: rolling back batching now.
```
# rollback snippet
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/kv-prefix-service KV_PREFIX_TTL=300
apply config: continuous_batching.window_ms=50 -> 200
```
Anna: rollback applied at 3654321058.
Devon: autoscaler up to 16 nodes now, new nodes joining.
Oliver: prefix_cache_hitrate creeping up 13% -> 48% after the rollback. queue_len starting to drop.
Mia: good. how about throttles and 429s?
Oliver: throttles trending down: 2.1 -> 0.2 req/s. 429s mostly cleared in last 90s.
CS-Bot: Customer-facing impact: estimated 30-min window of degraded latency for ~12 customers; 3 customers saw intermittent errors. recommend targeted notification and AM update.
Mia: @CS-Bot file a short incident message for affected customers: root cause change to batching/prefix-tll causing cache evaporation + autoscaler cap. say mitigation: rollback batching and temporary scale increase. ETA for full return: monitoring > 20m baseline.
CS-Bot: drafted. sending to support for review.
Devon: suggest follow-up items: (1) add autoscaler safety override that can be triggered by oncall without full infra deploy, (2) add canary gating for prefix cache changes, (3) add alert for sudden prefix cache hitrate drop.
Mia: agree. assign owners: Devon on autoscaler override, Anna on canary gating for cache-related flags, Oliver on alerting + dashboards.
Anna: will open PRs by EOD. also we should add a guard to not change both continuous batching and prefix TTL in same rollout.
Mia: nice. one more verification — can we run a live test load to confirm steady-state?
Oliver: running a small replay against canary traffic. results in next 5m.
incident-bot: NOTE: incident severity set to SEV3 (customer-impacting, limited surface). Pager escalation paused; oncall remains engaged.
Oliver: replay looks clean. tail latencies back to ~150ms; throughput back to baseline.
Mia: thanks all. summary for postmortem: root cause = rollout changed continuous batching and prefix TTL together which caused prefix cache "evaporation" under production traffic profile; autoscaler was constrained by a hard cap which prevented rapid scaling. mitigations applied: rolled back batching changes, temporarily increased max_nodes, monitored recovery. customer impact: short window (~30m) with elevated latencies and small fraction of 429s for a subset of customers. action items assigned.
Mia: I'll create the incident doc and tag owners. close thread when doc is up. :shipit:
Anna: I'll start the rollback postmortem notes in docs.
Devon: I'll schedule a quick sync with infra to discuss the autoscaler override.
CS-Bot: Customer messages queued for review.
Mia: closing active mitigation — monitoring for 20m, then post-incident writeup. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
